contracts.setup: A selected check launches a descendant that writes a readiness marker and heartbeat while inheriting stdout/stderr. A second selected check would write an unexpected marker.
contracts.stimulus: After descendant readiness, send SIGINT to the CLI. Separately, allow the immediate parent to exit zero while its descendant retains both pipes.
assertions: Interrupt: CLI completes within 5 seconds with status 130, records cancelled then skipped(reason=cancelled), and never runs the second check.
Exited parent: CLI completes within 5 seconds with status 0, drains/closes pipes, and both checks record passed.
In both cases descendant heartbeat stops after CLI completion; fixture cleanup targets only recorded owned PIDs.
POSIX process-group behavior is verified separately from Windows. Windows descendant cleanup is a Go target requirement, not an established Python guarantee.

contracts.setup: Generate a synthetic legacy workspace and record original managed state/source bytes. Provide an injectable planning seam that changes the state after reading it but before apply writes.
contracts.stimulus: Attempt update --apply after the concurrent change.
assertions: Return an explicit state-changed error, do not install relocated destination skills, and do not overwrite the concurrent state.
Go tests must also exercise observed file, legacy-tree, and report changes at preflight recheck seams. These are additional requirements beyond the existing single state-race test.

contracts.setup: Generate a legacy workspace and snapshot its state and original source files. Inject a first-write OSError in the existing atomic-write seam.
contracts.stimulus: Apply a legacy migration with the write failure enabled.
assertions: Surface the I/O failure; original state and legacy sources remain byte-identical.
Do not claim transactional apply: later I/O failures may leave new files before state is saved. Go must document and test its chosen write/retirement order.
Never retire customized, missing, or unmanaged sources to work around a failed update.

contracts.setup: Generate synthetic legacy runtime/rules/skills/catalogue trees with manifest-owned baselines; preserve a custom registry, actual project, local evidence, and historical report bytes.
contracts.stimulus: Preview, apply, and preview again. Repeat with edited/missing sources, destination collisions, unknown/unmanaged files, customized embedded skills, old report settings, and symlinks.
assertions: Clean previews are read-only; successful apply relocates owned files, retires only eligible catalogue copies, moves reports without changing bytes, and leaves no further actions.
Preserve user registry, project files, local evidence, root collection docs, and unknown non-managed content.
Any preflight conflict blocks all apply writes; --keep cannot bypass relocation or destination conflicts.
Installed CLI validates/guidance-checks the migrated workspace and generates another independent workspace.

contracts.setup: Customize managed README bytes and explicitly omit apps/.gitkeep and packages/README.md in template state; remove the apps marker but retain customized package bytes.
contracts.stimulus: Preview/apply with explicit --keep for eligible customizations, repeat preview, then generate a child using the installed CLI.
assertions: Keep preserves original baseline hashes and customized bytes; later previews still expose the customization.
Omitted homes stay omitted without deleting existing contents. Persist omissions without making them child-generation defaults.
Invalid omissions fail before any writes.
Retire obsolete unchanged bundled collection READMEs without removing the user's root homes; customized obsolete catalogue files block retirement.

contracts.setup: Generate workspaces with selected and unselected collections; include former defaults, custom root contents, and old embedded catalogue files.
contracts.stimulus: List, preview, apply, update, and generate a child with explicit selections. Repeat with invalid state, missing selected files, unmanaged existing scaffolds, symlinks, and file parents.
assertions: Preview is read-only; exclusive creation never adopts identical unmanaged files or overwrites existing bytes.
Any collision blocks the whole addition; already-managed selections remain untouched and apply is idempotent.
Selections persist through updates but do not implicitly propagate to generated children.
Unselected former defaults become preserved orphans, while only unchanged obsolete embedded copies retire.

contracts.setup: Generate a workspace with workspace-owned and independent project starters. Explicitly initialize their Git repositories and ignore only the independent project path at the workspace root.
contracts.stimulus: Register projects, run selected checks and guidance, generate editor output, and inspect parent staging. Verify root/template rules, skills, local links, and license notices.
assertions: Workspace-owned project files are eligible for parent staging; independent project files are absent from parent staging and retain their own Git root.
Generation does not initialize Git, install dependencies/clients, or require AI/container/editor integration.
Guidance remains self-contained; canonical/bundled skill and rule bytes, routes, names, and license notices match.
Malformed metadata, escaping/broken references, and legacy coexistence produce findings. Structural checks do not certify live client discovery.

contracts.setup: Select literal argument-array checks that fail, report findings, skip, overflow stdout/stderr, time out, or fail to launch; place a synthetic canary in output, arguments, and environment.
contracts.stimulus: Execute selected checks, inspect report JSON and captured terminal output, and vary effective configuration.
assertions: Preserve command ordering, literal arguments, required/report modes, finding-code classification, explicit skips, and configured limits.
Drain both streams while retaining only the configured prefix; preserve total output byte counts and truncation status.
Reports omit stdout/stderr, raw argv, and environment values; input and command hashes remain exact.
Reject invalid config and escaped/symlinked report roots before launching commands.
Exclusive report creation uses mode 0600 where supported; Go must specify Windows permissions and truthful runtime/schema metadata separately.
